simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-01.title: Count row by row
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-01.body:
- Top row: 6 pairs = $6 \times 2 = 12$ dots.
- Bottom row: also 12 dots.
- The two middle rows: 7 dots each = 14 dots.

Total: $12 + 12 + 14 = 38$.

**Answer: (B) 38**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-01.title: Count by columns
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-01.body:
There are 7 columns of 2 side dots ($7 \times 2 = 14$ dots). Between neighbouring columns there are 6 gaps, each with 2 dots on top and 2 dots at the bottom ($6 \times 4 = 24$ dots).

Total: $14 + 24 = 38$.

**Answer: (B) 38**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-02.title: Find the repeating block
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-02.body:
Name the shapes: T = tulip, P = five-petal flower with a dot, F = frilly flower, R = rose, S = six-petal flower. The row reads

T, P, F, **?**, S, T, P, **?**, R, S.

The block T, P, F, R, S repeats (the end of the row shows R just before S). So the first ? is R (rose) and the second ? is F (frilly flower).

**Answer: (D)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-02.title: Check each option
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-02.body:
Put each pair of shapes into the gaps and read the row: only with option D does the same block of five shapes (tulip, five-petal flower, frilly flower, rose, six-petal flower) repeat twice.

**Answer: (D)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-03.title: List the months
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-03.body:
- 31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October, December.
- 28 or 29 days: February.
- 30 days: April, June, September, November.

That is 4 months.

**Answer: (A) 4**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-03.title: Knuckle trick
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-03.body:
Count months on your knuckles: knuckles are 31-day months and the dips between them are the short months. The dips are February, April, June, September and November; February is not 30, leaving 4.

**Answer: (A) 4**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-04.title: Match the bumps
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-04.body:
The key has 3 teeth on one side and 1 tooth on the other side. The keyhole must have the same notches: 3 on one side, 1 on the other, with the single notch sitting between the two largest notches on the other side. Only the lock on chest E matches.

**Answer: (E)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-04.title: Rule out
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-04.body:
Check the keyholes one by one: A, B, C and D each have the wrong number or position of notches compared with the key's teeth, so they cannot fit. Only E is left.

**Answer: (E)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-05.title: Look at the jumps
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-05.body:
The numbers go down by $3, 6, 9, 12$ — each jump is 3 more than the one before. The next jump is 15:

$17 - 15 = 2$.

**Answer: (D) 2**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-06.title: Model method
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-06.body:
Let the red dress be 1 unit. The blue dress is 1 unit + \$100.

2 units + \$100 = \$110, so 2 units = \$10 and 1 unit = \$5.

**Answer: (B) \$5**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-06.title: Check the tempting answer
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-06.body:
If the red dress were \$10, the blue one would be \$110 and the total \$120 — too much. With \$5: blue is \$105, total \$110. ✓

**Answer: (B) \$5**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-07.title: Count stack by stack
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-07.body:
Count the height of each stack (column) of cubes, from left to right: 2, 4, 5 and 7 cubes (the hidden cubes underneath and behind must be there because there are no gaps).

Total: $2 + 4 + 5 + 7 = 18$.

**Answer: (C) 18**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-07.title: Count layer by layer
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-07.body:
Count the cubes on each level, remembering that every cube above must stand on cubes below. Adding up the layers from the bottom to the top again gives 18 cubes.

**Answer: (C) 18**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-08.title: Step by step
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-08.body:
Samuel now: $7 + 5 = 12$. David now: $12 + 2 = 14$. In 4 years: $14 + 4 = 18$.

18 is not among A–D.

**Answer: (E) None of the above**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-08.title: Add all the changes
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-08.body:
Start from Samuel 5 years ago (7). Going to 4 years from now adds $5 + 4 = 9$ years, and David is 2 years older: $7 + 9 + 2 = 18$.

**Answer: (E) None of the above**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-09.title: Compare the pictures
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-09.body:
The second plate is the first plate plus a pear, so the pear is $22 - 14 = 8$.

The third plate is apple + pear = 11, so the apple is $11 - 8 = 3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-09.title: Find the pomegranate first
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-09.body:
Plate 2 is plate 3 plus a pomegranate, so the pomegranate is $22 - 11 = 11$. From plate 1, apple $= 14 - 11 = 3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-10.title: The difference does not change
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-10.body:
Both sold 5 apples, so Daniel still has 6 fewer than Laura.

Let Daniel have 1 unit now; Laura has 1 unit + 6. Then 2 units + 6 = 36, so 2 units = 30 and 1 unit = 15.

**Answer: (B) 15**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-10.title: Make them equal
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-10.body:
If Laura gave away her 6 extra apples, they would have $36 - 6 = 30$ apples, shared equally: 15 each. That is Daniel's number.

**Answer: (B) 15**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-11.title: Change everything into coffee pots
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-11.body:
Third row: 1 coffee pot = 3 cups.

Second row: kettle = 3 coffee pots + 3 cups = 3 coffee pots + 1 coffee pot = 4 coffee pots. So 4 coffee pots = 1200 ml and 1 coffee pot = 300 ml, 1 cup = 100 ml.

First row: stewpan = kettle + coffee pot + cup = $1200 + 300 + 100 = 1600$ ml.

**Answer: (C) 1600 ml**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-11.title: Everything in cups
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-11.body:
1 coffee pot = 3 cups, so the kettle = $3 \times 3 + 3 = 12$ cups = 1200 ml, so 1 cup = 100 ml. The stewpan = $12 + 3 + 1 = 16$ cups = 1600 ml.

**Answer: (C) 1600 ml**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-12.title: Each feature appears once per row
Colours only
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-12.body:
Each row has one blue, one red and one yellow (star-shaped) flower, and one dotted, one white and one brown (shaded) pot. The last row already has a red flower in a white pot and a blue flower in a dotted pot, so the missing plant has a **yellow star flower in a brown pot**. Only C has that.

**Answer: (C)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-13.title: Multiples of 15
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-13.body:
A number divisible by both 3 and 5 is a multiple of 15. Two-digit multiples of 15: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90. The even ones are 30, 60, 90.

**Answer: (A) 3**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-13.title: Multiples of 30
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-13.body:
Even and divisible by 3 and 5 means divisible by $2 \times 3 \times 5 = 30$. Two-digit multiples of 30: 30, 60, 90 — three numbers.

**Answer: (A) 3**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-14.title: Try who is in primary 4
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-14.body:
The primary 4 girl is not Camila (she sits on Camila's left), so she is Aria or Evelyn.

- If Evelyn is primary 4, she is on Camila's left, so Aria is on Camila's right and Evelyn is on Aria's right. But the girl on Aria's right is the primary 3 girl — a contradiction.
- So Aria is primary 4 and sits on Camila's left. Then Camila is on Aria's right, so Camila is primary 3.

Evelyn is primary 2.

**Answer: (B) Evelyn**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-14.title: Draw the table
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-14.body:
Draw three seats in a circle. Put Camila anywhere; the seat on her left is primary 4. The primary 3 girl is on Aria's right, so Aria is not primary 3. Trying both ways to seat Aria and Evelyn, only Aria = P4 (on Camila's left) and Camila = P3 (on Aria's right) works, leaving Evelyn as P2.

**Answer: (B) Evelyn**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-15.title: Describe the two faces
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-15.body:
The pyramid shows two faces:

- Face 1: a dot on top of the hat, a white dot on the left of the nose, eyes looking right.
- Face 2: no dot on the hat, a white dot on the left of the nose, eyes looking right, and a bow tie.

Check each net for two neighbouring triangles with exactly these faces in the right positions. Only net E has both faces.

**Answer: (E)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-15.title: Rule out by details
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-15.body:
In nets A–D, one of the two faces always has a wrong detail (the dot on the hat missing or extra, eyes looking the wrong way, or the bow tie in the wrong place). Only E has both faces correct.

**Answer: (E)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-17.title: Count by number of parts
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-17.body:
Count the triangles by how many small regions they are made of:

- made of 1 part: 5
- made of 2 parts: 6
- made of 3 parts: 2
- made of 4 parts: 1

Total: $5 + 6 + 2 + 1 = 14$.

**Answer: 14**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-17.title: Count by corners
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-17.body:
Every triangle needs three corners joined by straight lines. Go through the points one at a time (top points first) and list every triangle having that point as its top corner, without repeating. The lists give 14 different triangles.

**Answer: 14**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-18.title: Count the pictures
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-18.body:
Chocolate Chip 7, Oatmeal Raisin 4, Peanut Butter 3, Almond 6 pictures: $7 + 4 + 3 + 6 = 20$ pictures.

Each picture is 7 cookies: $20 \times 7 = 140$.

**Answer: 140**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-19.title: Group the thirteens
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-19.body:
3 groups of 13 plus 5 groups of 13 is 8 groups of 13: $8 \times 13 = A \times 8$, so $A = 13$.

**Answer: 13**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-20.title: Fewest digits first
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-20.body:
A number with fewer digits is smaller, so use digits that need many matchsticks. The digit 8 uses the most, 7 matchsticks. Three digits use at most $3 \times 7 = 21 < 27$ sticks, so we need at least 4 digits.

With 4 digits: three 8s use 21 sticks, leaving 6 sticks for one more digit: 0, 6 or 9. The number cannot start with 0, so put the smallest allowed first digit in front: 6, giving 6888.

Could the first digit be smaller? A first digit 1–5 uses at most 5 sticks, leaving at least 22 sticks for three digits, but three digits use at most 21. So the first digit is at least 6, and 6888 is the smallest.

**Answer: 6888**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-20.title: Check the stick count
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-20.body:
Stick counts: 0→6, 1→2, 2→5, 3→5, 4→4, 5→5, 6→6, 7→3, 8→7, 9→6. For 6888: $6 + 7 + 7 + 7 = 27$. ✓ Any 4-digit number starting with 6 that is smaller (like 6088) uses fewer than 27 sticks, because 8 is the only digit with 7 sticks.

**Answer: 6888**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-21.title: Use the clues in order
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-21.body:
The greatest 1-digit number is 9, so the hundreds digit is 9.

Two digits adding to 15: 6 + 9 or 7 + 8. 9 is already used, so the tens and ones digits are 7 and 8.

The number is even, so it ends in 8: **978**.

**Answer: 978**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-21.title: Check
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-21.body:
978: digits all different ✓, hundreds digit 9 ✓, $7 + 8 = 15$ ✓, ends in 8 so even ✓. (987 is odd, 969 and 996 repeat digits.)

**Answer: 978**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-22.title: Groups of three numbers
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-22.body:
Three different numbers from 1–6 adding to 12: $\{1,5,6\}$, $\{2,4,6\}$, $\{3,4,5\}$. Each group can be put on the three coloured dice in $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ orders. Total $3 \times 6 = 18$.

**Answer: 18**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-23.title: Suppose all are chickens
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-23.body:
8 chickens would have $8 \times 2 = 16$ legs. There are $26 - 16 = 10$ extra legs. Each cow has 2 more legs than a chicken, so there are $10 \div 2 = 5$ cows and $8 - 5 = 3$ chickens.

**Answer: 3**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-23.title: Make a table
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-23.body:
Chickens 3, cows 5: $6 + 20 = 26$ legs ✓. (Chickens 4, cows 4 gives 24; chickens 2, cows 6 gives 28.)

**Answer: 3**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-24.title: Think of the unluckiest case
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-24.body:
In the worst case she first takes all $11 + 7 = 18$ green and yellow apples. After that every apple is red, so 3 more give 3 red apples: $18 + 3 = 21$.

With only 20 apples she might have just 2 red ones (18 others + 2 red), so 21 is needed.

**Answer: 21**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-24.title: Count what can go wrong
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-24.body:
To fail, she can hold at most all 18 non-red apples and 2 red ones, that is 20 apples. One more apple, the 21st, guarantees 3 red.

**Answer: 21**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-25.title: Start from the front
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-25.body:
A 3-digit number plus a 2-digit number is less than 1100, so the 4-digit answer starts with 1: $R = 1$.

Ones: $R + R = 2$, so $F = 2$.

The result is 1EE2 with no carry from the ones. For the hundreds to reach 10, the tens must carry 1, so $C + 1 = 10 + E$: $C = 9$, $E = 0$. Tens: $O + O = 10 + E = 10$, so $O = 5$.

Check: $951 + 51 = 1002$. ✓

**Answer: 1002**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-25.title: Size argument
simcc-sasmo-2020-g2-25.body:
COR + OR is between 1000 and 1098, so REEF starts with 10: $R = 1$, $E = 0$, and $F = 1 + 1 = 2$. So REEF = 1002 (indeed $951 + 51 = 1002$).

**Answer: 1002**
